lots.guide_summary: Close same-region evidence runs $200 to $450 hammer from five Gowans Hamadan runner SOLD results (Nov 2025 to Jun 2026), all about 3 m long like this lot. Retail ASKING prices for Hossainabad runners are $1,305 (AU), $1,650 (AU, 4.4 m) and GBP 1,535 (about AUD 3,145 at 2.05, 3.95 m). Category guides (Baluchi, Meshwani, unnamed 3 m) sold $90 to $240, with two UNSOLD re-offers. No Armitage past result found. Auction reality is the SOLD band, not the retail figures.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD = $200 (Gowans Hamadan 292 x 102, Nov 2025, within 24 months). Treating Gowans hammer as the price paid (conservative, their premium is extra). 200 / 1.22 = 163.9, round down to $160 hammer (all-in $195.20). Flip: likely resale = median of the five Hamadan SOLD hammers ($200, $220, $280, $320, $450) = $280, resold through a local auction room. Less about 15% seller's commission ($42) and $0 postage (local consignment) = $238. 238 / 2.44 = 97.5, round down to $95 hammer. This lot is narrower (85 cm vs 100 to 115 cm) so area is smaller, supporting the lower figures.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification is clear from the design and Armitage's own description (307 x 85 cm, hand knotted Hossainabad), and five close SOLD results were confirmed in the Gowans API. Not High because there is no woven or printed mark to read in the photos, the Gowans comps are Hamadan generally rather than Hossainabad by name, and condition is from studio photos only.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped outright. Corrected: RugMaster price is $1,650 on the opened page, not the $1,499 snippet; Little Persia is GBP 1,535 (not $1,768, currency unknown), now converted. Added Gowans 3 m Persian runner $160 (id 372249) and the Meshwani unsold (367244) as an UNSOLD entry rather than folded into a SOLD range.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos: full length flat shot, angled shot and close-up of the field. All-over small herati/boteh style motifs on a salmon-red field, cream border with dark scroll pattern, light blue corner spandrels at each end. Pile looks full and even, colours bright, fringe ends visible and intact. Photos look like dealer studio shots on a white background, so wear may be hidden. No label or tag visible.
lots.condition: Appears good to very good: full pile, clean colours, intact fringes, no visible holes or repairs in the photos (studio photography, unverified).
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you confirm the size (307 x 85 cm) and that it is hand knotted (check knots on the back), and whether there are any worn patches, moth damage, stains or re-done fringes? Is the documentation of authenticity from an importer, and is the rug clean?

lots.guide_summary: All evidence is other Naughton works, no result for this painting. Within 24 months: 6 SOLD from $130 to $750 (figurative/stockmen scenes $260 to $750, median about $330 across all six), 2 UNSOLD ceilings at $300 and $325 last bid including a campfire subject. No ASKING entries. Older results ($260 to $550) are background only. All AUD. Invaluable does not say if priceResult includes premium; Lawsons figures equal the last bid so are probably hammer.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD within 24 months for a figurative Naughton = $260 (The Fossicker, Lawsons, 2026-06-03). Treated as all-in to be safe. 260 / 1.22 = 213.1, round down to $210 hammer (all-in $256.20). The $130 eagle is a weaker subject, filed as category guide, not used. Flip: likely resale = median of the six 24-month SOLD results ($130, $260, $300, $360, $600, $750) = $330, call it $360 for a figurative stockmen scene that is wider than most (35 x 75). Less about 15% seller's commission ($54), $0 postage (consign locally or to Lawsons with buyer freight) = $306. 306 / 2.44 = 125.4, round down to $125 hammer.
lots.confidence_reason: Armitage catalogues it as Keith Naughton with a title, and the lower right signature is a long cursive scrawl consistent with 'Naughton' but not clearly readable at this resolution. The loose night-scene style is less typical of his daylight outback scenes. Many SOLD results were opened and parsed, but none is this painting, and premium inclusion is unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped; all researcher prices, dates and estimates matched the Invaluable JSON. Reclassified the 2024 and earlier sales as background only (outside 24 months). Noted that two older priceResults (Danielle Elizabeth 360 vs bid 280, Leonard Joel 550 vs bid 360) may include premium.
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos. Night scene: five or six stockmen in hats squatting and kneeling around a fire with a billy and rising smoke, horses and figures faint in the dark background, warm orange ground. Long panoramic format (about 35 x 75 cm). Signature lower right in light paint, a long cursive scrawl, plausibly 'Naughton', not fully legible. Two small white labels on the mount below, one may read 'Keith Naughton' (not legible enough to confirm). Glazed or unglazed not clear. Frame shows no obvious damage.
lots.condition: Appears sound: no visible flaking, tears or stains in the photos; frame and mount look clean. Medium (board or canvas) and back not seen.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a title or gallery label on the back confirming Keith Naughton and 'Get a Move On Cook', and is the support board or canvas? Please confirm the signature reads Naughton and check for any paint loss or foxing to the mount.

Goldstein badges on doors and an orange Goldstein plate on each control panel; 'Rapid Fry' script; red rocker switch, 'IMPORTANT safety instruction' panel about solid shortening, Caho digital thermostat with dial on each unit.
